content: The test image shows green banana fruits with dark brown/black necrotic tissue at their blossom (tip) ends. This pattern — dry, shriveled, dark rot at the distal tip of each banana finger — is the hallmark of Cigar End Rot. Now I'll view one reference image to confirm.

The reference image confirms it perfectly. Both images show:
- Black/brown necrosis starting at the blossom (perianth) end of immature banana fingers
- Dry, shriveled dark tissue adhering to the tip (resembling cigar ash)
- Multiple fingers in a cluster affected simultaneously

This is a textbook match for Cigar End Rot caused by *Verticillium theobromae* / *Trachysphaera fructigena*.
